queries.need: When a token fails verification because its expiration time has passed, I want an error I can recognize, with the expiry timestamp available so I can report when it expired.

When a token is malformed, has a bad signature, is missing a signature, or fails audience, issuer, subject, or ID checks, I want a general error type with a descriptive message so I can reject the token and explain why.
When a token is presented before its not-before time, I want a specific error that tells me the token isn't active yet and includes the date it becomes valid.
I need to generate a short, unique string identifier for each new record I create, something URL-friendly and compact that is safe to use across multiple server processes without collisions.

I have a bunch of promise-returning tasks and want to run them so that only a fixed number execute at the same time, starting new ones as earlier ones finish, while still getting all their results together.

I want to create a limiter with a concurrency setting that I can pass either as a plain number or as an options object, and I want pending tasks to reject with an abort-style error when I clear the waiting queue so that my awaited Promise.all doesn't hang.

I have one async function that gets called many times, for example in a loop, and I want the function itself to never run more than a set number of instances at once, without setting up a separate limiter at each call site.
I need to cap how many times a function can run within a rolling time window, such as at most 5 calls every second, and have extra calls wait their turn instead of failing.
I want the rate limit enforced strictly for every individual call, so that no sliding time window ever exceeds my maximum count, even if that costs more processing overhead.
I want to cancel all calls that are still waiting in the throttle queue when I abort a controller, with those pending calls rejecting using the abort reason I provide.
I want to be notified with the arguments whenever a call has to be held back because the rate limit was reached, so I can monitor how often throttling happens.
I need each call to consume a different share of the rate limit based on its arguments, for example an API where some requests cost more quota points than others.
I have a version string with stray whitespace, a leading equals sign, or a leading 'v'. I want it cleaned up into a plain version number.
I need to check whether a specific version falls within a range expression that combines alternatives, hyphen ranges, and wildcards.
I need to know whether one version is strictly newer than another.
I need to know whether one version is strictly older than another.
Given a range like '>=1.0.0', I want the lowest version that satisfies it.
I have a messy string like 'v2' or '42.6.7.9.3-alpha' that is not strictly valid, and I want to extract the closest proper version from it.
I want to pick only the versions out of a list that match a range, and get the highest one.
I want to pick only the versions out of a list that match a range, and get the lowest one.
I want to turn a range expression into its individual comparator pieces so I can inspect them.
I need to check whether a version is greater than every version in a range.
I need to check whether a version is less than every version in a range.
I need to know whether two ranges have any version in common.
I need to know whether every version accepted by one range is also accepted by another range.
I want to bump a version by major, minor, patch, or prerelease level, optionally with a custom prerelease identifier.
I want to know which part of a version changed between two versions, such as major, minor, patch, or prerelease.
I want to parse a version string into an object whose fields I can read and modify, including prerelease and build parts.
I want to compare versions in a relaxed way that tolerates minor formatting differences.
I want to compare versions including their build metadata as a tiebreaker.
I have a list of version strings and want them sorted from oldest to newest, or newest to oldest.
I want to check whether two versions are equal, or not equal, using the version precedence rules.
I want to shorten a version to a given number of leading components, such as just major or major.minor.
I want to bump a version and attach a prerelease label such as beta, so 1.2.3 becomes 1.2.4-beta.0.
I want to step through a prerelease series by bumping an existing prerelease version like 1.2.4-beta.0 to 1.2.4-beta.1, and then finalize it to the plain release 1.2.4.
I want to bump a version string to its next prerelease, using a label like beta, and choose whether the counter starts at zero or one, or leave the number off entirely.
I want to bump a version string to the next major, minor, or patch release, or to a prerelease of the next version, optionally with a custom label, and get nothing back if the input is invalid.
I want to know whether two version ranges or comparators overlap, meaning some version satisfies both.
I want to convert a string into a structured version object, or get nothing if it isn't a valid version.
I want to strip a version down to a given level, such as removing prerelease and build info and zeroing lower components when keeping only major or minor, without changing the higher components.
I want to test whether one version is greater than another, using semantic version precedence rather than string comparison.
I want to test whether one version is greater than or equal to another by semantic precedence.
I want to test whether one version is less than another by semantic precedence.
I want to test whether one version is less than or equal to another by semantic precedence.
I want to check whether two version strings are logically equal even if written differently, and also check that they are not equal.
I want to check whether two versions are logically different, the opposite of checking equality.

I want to apply a comparison operator given as a text symbol to two versions and get a boolean, with an error if the symbol is unrecognized; symbols for plain string equality and inequality should also work.
I want a three-way comparison of two versions returning 0, 1, or -1, which I can pass to a sort to order versions ascending.
I want a reverse three-way comparison of two versions so that sorting produces a descending list.
I want to compare two versions where build metadata breaks ties when their precedence is otherwise equal, and use that to sort ascending.
I want to compare two version strings in a lenient way that tolerates slightly malformed input.
I want to find out what kind of change separates two versions, such as major, minor, patch, or prerelease, or learn that they are the same.
I have a list of version strings and want them ordered from lowest to highest, using build metadata as a tiebreaker.
I have a list of version strings and want them ordered from highest to lowest, using build metadata as a tiebreaker.
I want to know whether two individual comparators, such as a bound like '>=1.2.3' and another like '<2.0.0', overlap so that some version could satisfy both.
I have a version range written as a string and want to check whether it is syntactically valid, getting back a normalized form if it is or nothing if it is not.
I have a single version and a range string, and I want a yes or no answer on whether that version falls within the range.
I have a list of versions and a range, and I want the highest version in the list that falls within the range, or nothing if none qualify.
I have a list of versions and a range, and I want the lowest version in the list that falls within the range, or nothing if none qualify.
Given a range, I want to find the smallest version that could possibly match it, for example to set a minimum required version.
I want to check whether a version is higher than every version a given range could match, so I know it is newer than the whole range.
I want to check whether a version is lower than every version a given range could match, so I know it is older than the whole range.

I want to know whether a version lies entirely above or entirely below a range, choosing the direction with a '>' or '<' argument, since the range may have gaps so being above or below is not the same as not matching.
I have a range and want to know whether any of its comparators overlap with each other, meaning the range has at least some version that could be allowed.
I have two ranges and want to confirm that every version allowed by the first one is also allowed by the second one.

I have a version string with stray whitespace, an equals sign, or a 'v' prefix, and I want it normalized to a plain valid version, or null if it can't be made valid; I may also want a lenient mode that tolerates sloppy prerelease formatting.

I have a unique identifier written as a 36-character hyphenated hex string, and I need its 16 raw bytes as a byte array in the same left-to-right order the hex digits appear. If the string isn't a valid identifier, I want an error thrown.

I have 16 bytes stored in an array-like collection, possibly starting at some offset within a larger buffer, and I need them converted into the standard hyphenated hex identifier string. If the bytes can't produce a valid identifier, I want an error.

I want to generate a time-based unique identifier, and optionally control the node field, clock sequence, timestamp, and sub-millisecond offset, or supply my own random bytes or random generator. I also want the result written directly into a byte buffer at a given offset when I need binary output instead of a string.
I have existing version 1 identifiers and need them converted to the newer time-ordered version 6 layout so the timestamp bits sort correctly, without changing the rest of the value.
I want a deterministic identifier derived from a name and a namespace using MD5 hashing, so the same inputs always produce the same identifier, optionally written into a byte buffer at an offset.
I need a random unique identifier, optionally seeded with my own 16 random bytes or a random generator function, and I want the option to write its binary form into a buffer at a chosen offset.
I have existing version 6 UUIDs stored in my system and need to convert them back to version 1 format.
I need to accept only UUIDs of one specific version, like v4, and reject valid UUIDs of other versions.
I am generating timestamp-based UUIDs and want to pass my own options without those options disturbing the uniqueness guarantees across calls.
I want to check that some untrusted input matches the shape I expect, and get back a typed, validated copy of it that I can use safely; if the input is wrong, I need an error instead.
I have a validation rule that has to wait on something asynchronous, like a lookup or network check, and I need a way to run validation that returns a promise so I can await the result.
I need to add a custom check to a string schema, such as a maximum length enforced by an async function, without rewriting the whole schema.
